title: Edit V-Ray Render Properties
content: ### **Objective** Configure render properties for the final render image. ### **Location** Render Toolbar ▶ ![render_properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36781019890457) Render Properties. ### **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu in Location. → Render properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Refer to the below table and edit the settings as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Render Engine** | **Render Engine** | Choose the computer engine to run the render. **CPU** | Run the render with CPU. **GPU (CUDA)** | Run the render with GPU (CUDA). **GPU (OpenCL)** | Run the render with GPU (OpenCL). **CPU Supporting** | Use CPU along with GPU when rendering. Toggle off this option to not use CPU. **📝****Note:** This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as GPU (CUDA). **Low GPU Priority** | Lower GPU priority when rendering. GPU is firstly used in other functions and then used in render. **📝****Note:** This option only appears when Render Engine is selected as either GPU (CUDA) or GPU (OpenCL). **Finish Conditions** | **Noise Threshold** | Set the Noise Threshold for the final render image. The default value is 0.050 and the range is between 0.001 and 0.100. The higher the Noise Threshold is, the more the noise is in the final render image. **Max, Render Time (min)** | The time used for rendering is about two minutes on average when default settings are used for render, light, and image/video properties. However, any modification on the properties may alter the render time. With this option, decide the maximum time that can be used for rendering per image. **Quality** | Adjust the render quality of lights and materials. The Quality can be adjusted to four levels: Low, Medium, High, and Very High. As the option is set towards Very High, render speed decreases. **📝****Note:** * Increase the Quality to render white fur. * Increase the Quality to express light reflections more realistically when textures are added to the studio environment such as the wall and floor. **Light** | Adjust the quality of the light. **Material** | Adjust the quality of materials. **Mesh Optimization** **(Final** **Render Only)** **** **** | **Knitwear** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40170473107609) Optimize the knitwear mesh in the invisible camera area of the final rendered image. This option only appears when Camera Lens is selected as Default. **Frustum Culling** | No knitwear mesh is created outside the view frustum. A minor difference may appear in the final rendered image when Frustum Culling is enabled. This setting removes all meshes that are out of the camera's view. **LOD** | Level of Detail. The number of knitwear meshes is reduced based on their distance from the camera, with greater distances resulting in fewer meshes. **Color Mapping** | Calibrate the final image color. **Type** **(ver 7.2**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142311561881)**](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=LlQ6koe3LMps8Meq&t=3057)**)** | Choose the type of Color Mapping. **Reinhard** | The closer the Burn value is to 1.0, the more the image color is multiplied simply by the brightness, and the closer it is to 0.0, the more the color is saturated by the brightness. **HSV exponential****** | Similar to Reinhard's Burn value of 0.0, the ratio of color (RGB) remains. **📝****Note:** * Use the **Open** , **Save** buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the setting. * To optimize the render speed, please refer to the below directions. 1\. When your OS is Windows: a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select **GPU (CUDA)** for **Engine** for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select **GPU (OpenCL)** for **Engine** for faster render time. 2\. When your OS is Mac:**( ver 2025.0**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142311561881)**](https://youtu.be/UI7jhqvsXdk?si=2K-0IJSklHU3Xw4c)[**)**](https://youtu.be/UI7jhqvsXdk?si=2K-0IJSklHU3Xw4c) a) and uses Nvidia for graphic card, select **GPU (CUDA)** for **Engine** for faster render time. b) and uses AMD or Intel for graphic card, select **CPU** for **Engine** for faster render time.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide to configuring render properties for optimal final image output in your rendering software.

content: **List of Contents** Move Zoom In/Out and Rotate Rotate Grainline Setting options **Objective** Modify the Fabric's grainline and location for individual Patterns, and texture image's rotation and size for individual Fabric. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Texture ▶ **Edit Texture** 2D/3D Toolbar ▶ ![_______2D___.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005711127) **Edit Texture** **Operation** **Move** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click ▶ Drag texture image applied to Pattern with the left mouse button. → The selected texture image of the selected Pattern is now being moved. **Zoom In/Out and Rotate** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Select a pattern with fabric applied. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. Click on the diagonal, vertical, horizontal lines of the gizmo ▶ drag, or drag along the gizmo circle. → Diagonal line : The size of the texture image is adjusted while the aspect ratio is maintained. → Horizontal/ Vertical: Texture images are scaled only in the vertical and horizontal directions. → Circle : The texture image is rotated. 4. Or select a Fabric and enter the image's [Width and Height](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011527274-Edit-Texture-Size-Property-Editor-) value in Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Texture** Transformation. **※ Note:** * Right-click to input the exact values while rotating textures and grainlines. * Edit back of texture when you change **Garment Rendering Style** as [Back Texture Surface.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011148874-2D-Window-Display-Icons-ver5-0-0-and-Above-) **Rotate Grainline** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Select a Pattern to rotate the Fabric. → A Gizmo is now being activated at the top-right corner of the 2D window. 3. A circle appears when mouse-over the curve. → Drag the grainline in the direction you want to rotate it. 4. Simulate once it is adjusted. → The draping is now being adjusted according to the change in grainline. **※ Note:** You can directly enter the angle in the Pattern Properties ▶ Fabric ▶ Grain Direction menu, and if you turn off the Link All Colorways menu, you can apply the different grain direction for each colorway. **Setting options** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the pattern and set options as needed. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Assign to New Fabric** | Apply new fabric to selected pattern. **Reset to Basic Fabric** | Reset the fabric of the selected pattern to the properties of the basic fabric. **Reset Fabric Angle** | Resets the texture angle to the original angle. **Align Grain** | Aligns the grainline at an angle parallel to the X, Y, or custom axis. **Match up Grain (ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142221677209)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=TlrDBg3s9NYN3N0U&t=3707)**)** | Align the grainline so that the texture between the selected segment and the baseline continues smoothly. For symmetrical patterns, the selected segment and symmetric line are matched. **Delete Texture** | Delete the texture. **Flip Texture Horizontally/ Vertically** | Flip the texture horizontally or vertically. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides essential instructions for modifying the grainline, rotation, and size of fabric textures for individual patterns within a design application.

title: Userpool Settings
content: ## **New in 2024.2** #### **List of Contents** Concept Instruction FAQ #### **Concept** #### **What is Userpool?** A Userpool is a list of Members authorized to use the Owner's license. The license Owner can add or delete Members' email(CLO-SET account) who are allowed to use the license. Once the Member is added to the Userpool, Members can sign in to the software using their own CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. By doing so, the Owner no longer needs to share the license ID and password, enhancing security and collaboration efficiency. #### **Who can use Userpool?** Any users with the licenses to sign in to CLO Network Onlineauth 2024.2 and later versions. #### **Where is Userpool provided?** The Userpool and a more detailed manual are provided in License Account Admin. Below is how you can access to the Userpool Settings page. Sign in clo3d.com > Click Account( ![account_icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945712495769) ) on the top right side > Sign in ![License account admin.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945720137497) > Click ![Userpool Setting.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945720141849) on the left side #### **** #### **Instruction** #### **How to ADD members to the Userpool** **From the Userpool Settings** Click ![Add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945712513433) and type the Member's email address. For better management, you can set a Member name when adding a member. The Member will receive an invitation email with the software installer included. **From the Software (Auto Add)** If the CLO-SET account is signed in from the software, the account will be automatically added as a Member to the Userpool list. The Owner will receive the notification email when the new Member is auto added. If the Owner doesn't want the Members to be auto added, Auto Add option can be turned off. #### #### **How to DELETE members from the Userpool** Mark the Members from the list > Click ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39109913714841) Deleted Members cannot sign in to the software with their CLO-SET account to use the Owner's license. Deleted Members can be added again whenever it's needed. #### **** #### **FAQ** **Can the license Owner be the Member of the other Userpool?** Yes. If the Owner's email has the CLO-SET account and that same account is invited to another Userpool, the account can also be a Member under another Userpool. **I am invited as a Userpool Member, but cannot sign in to the software.** The Member needs to be signed up to CLO-SET and have a CLO-SET account to sign in to the software. However, any email can be added when the Owner invites the Members. **Do the Userpool Owner and Member related to the CLO-SET group's admin and users(collaborator, editor, viewer)?** No, the Userpool is a separate feature from CLO-SET group permissions.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on the new Userpool feature in CLO Network Onlineauth 2024.2, detailing its purpose, usage instructions, and frequently asked questions to enhance user collaboration and security.

title: How to Create Fur: Material Type "Fur (Render Only)"
content: #### **List of Contents** Apply Fur Fur Parameters Fur Gradation Color Fur Base Fur Maps (+ Fur Cluster Generator) Fur Gravity Fur Curl Fur Variance #### **Fur (Render Only) is a material type through which you can visualize realistic fur, fleece, etc. It can be applied onto any component in your 3D window or Object Browser that shows a Property Editor with a material type option. (E.g. fabrics, buttons, trims, avatars...) ** **This material type is render only, which means it can only be previewed during[Interactive Render](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render). If you wish to preview fur in the 3D window, check out material type [Fur Strand](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/44205065227801-Create-Fur-Strand-Beta).** **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/47286526797721)** #### #### **Apply Fur** 1. [Change the Material Type](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-Material-Type) to **fur (render only)**. 2. If desired, select one of the presets to express fox, mink, angora, sherpa and more. #### #### **Fur Parameters** ** Option ** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- **Melanin** | Higher melanin value tints the color browner and darker. The lower the value, the more similar the color remains to the original color you set before. **Pheomelanin** | Higher pheomelanin value tints the fur redder. This value functions proportionally to the melanin value; the pheomelanin value is not taken into account when the melanin value is 0. **Glossiness** | Configure shininess of the fur. When light is shone onto the fur, a higher value makes it shinier. **Glossiness Boost** | Express coated fur. Glossiness adjusts intrinsic shininess of the fur whereas Glossiness Boost expresses the shininess from the fur finishing, like wax or coating. The higher the Glossiness Boost value is, the stronger the fur finishing effect appears. **Softness** | Express smoothness of the fur. Higher Softness value is makes the fur smoother. A lower makes it rougher. **Compensate Energy** | If light cannot pass through denser hair sufficiently, this compensates for a lack of light bounces throughout the affected area. #### #### **Fur Gradation Color** Click the check box to change any gradation properties. **Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Fur Gradation Color ** | ** Color ** | Select the mid and the tip color of the gradation. **Position** | Adjust the length of the fur where Mid and Tip Color is applied. ** Interpolation ** | Naturally blend the borders of tip, mid, and root colors. #### #### **Fur Base** ** Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- ** Length ** | Configure the length of the fur. A higher value corresponds to longer fur. Example: Length = **50 vs. 10** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033587) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033607) ** Thickness ** | Configure the thickness of a single thread of the fur. A higher value corresponds to thicker strands. Example: Thickness = **10 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956288) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033607) **Bend** | Configure the bending strength of the fur. A higher value causes the strands to be more affected by gravity, therefore bending more. Example: Bend = **1 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033807) ![Untitled_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033787) **Taper** | Differentiate the thickness of the fur between its root and the end. A higher value makes the strands become thinner towards their ends. A low value keeps a similar thickness between roots and ends. Example: Taper (with Thickness 2.00) = **1.00 vs. 0.00** ![Untitled_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956388) ![Untitled_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956448) **Density** | Configure how closely placed the strands are. Higher value corresponds to denser fur. Lower value gives a more scattered appearance. Example: Density = **1 vs. 0.20** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003033587) ![Untitled_6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956468) **Segments** | Configure how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into. When the fur is long and has a higher bending value, the fur must have a higher amount of segments to express the Bending smoothly and realistically. However, for short and straight fur, this value is not as significant. #### #### **Fur Maps** Use base maps to express different levels of length, thickness, density, curl, bend, gravity, bend direction, and initial direction within a single pattern piece. **Maps for bend, length, thickness, density, curl, and gravity, like roughness and metalness maps, use a monochrome image as input** , with the image’s color values serving as the multiplier for the bend parameter. 0 is multiplied to the values when a map is black, while 1 is multiplied to the values when a map is white. **Maps for initial direction and bend direction define the direction of the fur and, like normal maps, use an RGB image as input** in red, green, and blue tones. The initial direction map determines the direction in which the fur initially grows, while the bend direction map defines how the fur curves from root to tip. _ Example: ![map_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360017402834) _ ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475777301017) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475800641817) You can easily generate the realistic Fur Cluster by controlling the length and bend direction. 1. 1. Open the **Fur Cluster Generator** by clicking the ![Inner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39475777303833) button. 2. Generate the Fur Cluster. **Properties**** **| ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- ** Length ** ** ** ** ** | ** Cropping Map ** **** | Use the Cropping Map to apply different length within a single pattern piece. **Mode** | As a cropping map is grayscale, the length is determined based on the level of darkness (RGB) or the transparency (Alpha). Transparent and black areas have the lowest Length, while opaque and white areas have the highest Length. **Level** | Adjust intensity of gray tones. Increasing the value makes the cropping effect more obvious. **Low/High Length** | Adjust the shortest or longest fur length. ** Trimming ** ** ** | **Intensity** | Trim the length from the edge to the center of the fur cluster. Higher intensity increases the difference in fur length from the edge to the center to create a sharper fur. #### ![Fur Cluster_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510720113945) **Random** | Higher randomization makes the clumps irregular, while lower randomization makes the clumps consistent. ![Fur Cluster_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40718701504025) ** Bend Direction ** **** | ** Cluster ** | **Intensity** | Adjusts the intensity of the fur bending in each direction. Higher intensity makes the fur clump more pronounced and dimensional. ![Fur Cluster_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510720146713) **Pores Density** | Adjust the pores density of the fur cluster. Higher density makes the clumps smaller and tighter, while lower density makes the clumps larger and more spread out. ![Fur Cluster_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40153821981977) **Direction/****Intensity Random** | Adjust whether the bend direction is consistent or irregular. ** Detail Cluster ** | The clumping of smaller sub-units within the cluster can be adjusted in the same way as the cluster. **Relax** | Adjust the intensity of clumping in detail clusters while keeping each direction intact. Higher relaxation makes the clumps loosen smoothly, as if gently combed out. ![Fur Cluster_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39510741655705) #### #### **Fur Gravity** **Option** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- ** Force ** | Apply gravitational force. ** Vector ** | Manually apply a gravitational value to each axis. #### #### **Fur Curl** ** Option ** ** ** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Radius** | Configure the size of the curls. A higher value corresponds to larger curl and vice versa. Example (with Number 5.00): Radius = **5.00 vs. 1.00** ![Untitled_8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956808) ![Untitled_9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956828) **Number** | Configure the amount of curls. A higher value corresponds to more curls and vice versa. Example (with Radius 5.00): Number = **5.00 vs. 0.00** ![Untitled_8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956808) ![Untitled_9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002956828) #### #### **Fur Variance** ** Option ** ** ** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Length** | Express uniform or irregular fur length. A higher value corresponds to more irregular fur length; lower value results in more uniform length variety. **Thickness** | Express uniform or irregular fur thickness. A higher value corresponds to more irregular fur thickness is; lower value results in more uniform thickness. **Direction** | Express uniform or irregular fur bending direction. A higher value corresponds to more irregular direction; lower value results in more uniform direction. **Gravity** | Express a uniform or irregular gravitational effect. A higher value causes a more irregular effect; lower value results in a more uniform effect. _A value can only be applied here if the Bending value is not 0._ #### **Back to List of Contents**

title: How to Create Fur: Material Type "Fur_Strand" (Beta)
content: ## **New in CLO 2025.0** Apply Fur Strand Fur Strand Display in 3D Window Fur Strand Shape in 3D Window Fur Parameters Fur Gradation Color Fur Base Fur Maps Fur Gravity Fur Curl Fur Variance Fur Randomization Fur Export (USD) YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gqbgS7NQg6k?si=-WWorUiKkSDwKkey **Generate and preview realistic fur strands in the 3D window with various shapes and colors! ** **Share the same geometry on platforms that support Fur Strand, ensuring compatibility and flexibility across different applications.** **📝****Note:** * Fur Strand is initially available as a beta service only on Windows and will be generally released later based on your valuable feedback. * Rendered results of Fur Strand may differ slightly from existing Fur (Render Only). #### **Apply Fur Strand** 1. [Change the Material Type](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-Material-Type) to**Fur_Strand**. _* Fur can be previewed in 3D Window with Default Render, Quality Render, and [Interactive Render](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render). _ 2. Select one of the presets to express Fox, Mink, Angora, Sherpa, etc. #### **Set Fur Strand Display/Shape in 3D Window** 1. Hover over ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211384473)**3D Garment Display**. 2. Activate **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192147993)****Show Fur Strand** to show or hide in the 3D window. 3. Activate **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211386137)****Random Fur Strand Color** to randomize each fur strand's color. #### **Fur Strand Shape****in 3D Window** 1. Access Users Settings ▶ 3D ▶ Fur Strand Shape. 2. Select either Cylinder / Plane / Line shape. → Display Fur Strand in the selected shape in the 3D Window instantly. ** Option ** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- **Cylinder** | Display fur in a cylinder shape with thickness and width. **Plane** | Display fur in a plane shape without thickness but with width. **Line** | Display fur in spline curves without thickness or width. #### #### **Fur Parameters** ** Option ** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- **Melanin** | Higher melanin value tints the color browner and darker. The lower the value, the more similar the color remains to the original color you set before. **Pheomelanin** | Higher pheomelanin value tints the fur redder. This value functions proportionally to the melanin value; the pheomelanin value is not taken into account when the melanin value is 0. **Glossiness** | Configure shininess of the fur. When light is shone onto the fur, a higher value makes it shinier. **Glossiness Boost** | Express coated fur. Glossiness adjusts intrinsic shininess of the fur whereas Glossiness Boost expresses the shininess from the fur finishing, like wax or coating. The higher the Glossiness Boost value is, the stronger the fur finishing effect appears. **Softness** | Express smoothness of the fur. Higher Softness value is makes the fur smoother. A lower makes it rougher. **Compensate Energy** | If light cannot pass through denser hair sufficiently, this compensates for a lack of light bounces throughout the affected area. #### #### **Fur Gradation Color** Click the check box to change any gradation properties. **Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Fur Gradation Color ** | ** Color ** | Select the mid and the tip color of the gradation. **Position** | Adjust the length of the fur where Mid and Tip Color is applied. ** Interpolation ** | Naturally blend the borders of tip, mid, and root colors. #### #### **Fur Base** ** Option** | ** Description ** ---|--- ** Length ** | Configure the length of the fur. A higher value corresponds to longer fur. Example: Length = **50 vs. 10** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192151705) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192152345) ** Thickness ** | Configure the thickness of a single thread of the fur. A higher value corresponds to thicker strands. Example: Thickness = **10 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211389593) ![Untitled.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192152345) **Bend** | Configure the bending strength of the fur. A higher value causes the strands to be more affected by gravity, therefore bending more. Example: Bend = **1 vs. 0.20** ![Untitled_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192153753) ![Untitled_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192155673) **Taper** | Differentiate the thickness of the fur between its root and the end. A higher value makes the strands become thinner towards their ends. A low value keeps a similar thickness between roots and ends. Example: Taper (with Thickness 2.00) = **1.00 vs. 0.00** ![Untitled_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211391513) ![Untitled_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211392025) **Density** | Configure how closely placed the strands are. Higher value corresponds to denser fur. Lower value gives a more scattered appearance. Example: Density = **1 vs. 0.20** ![50.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192151705) ![Untitled_6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192157977) **Segments** | Configure how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into. When the fur is long and has a higher bending value, the fur must have a higher amount of segments to express the Bending smoothly and realistically. However, for short and straight fur, this value is not as significant. #### #### **Fur Maps** Use base maps to express different levels of length, thickness, density, curl, bend, gravity, bend direction, and initial direction within a single pattern piece. **Maps for bend, length, thickness, density, curl, and gravity, like roughness and metalness maps, use a monochrome image as input** , with the image’s color values serving as the multiplier for the bend parameter. 0 is multiplied to the values when a map is black, while 1 is multiplied to the values when a map is white. **Maps for initial direction and bend direction define the direction of the fur and, like normal maps, use an RGB image as input** in red, green, and blue tones. The initial direction map determines the direction in which the fur initially grows, while the bend direction map defines how the fur curves from root to tip. _ Example: ![map_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192158873) _ ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44205091519001) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52442249594137) You can easily generate the realistic Fur Cluster by controlling the length and bend direction. 1. 1. Open the **Fur Cluster Generator** by clicking the ![Inner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211395865) button. 2. Generate the Fur Cluster. **Properties**** **| ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- ** Length ** ** ** ** ** | ** Cropping Map ** **** | Use the Cropping Map to apply different length within a single pattern piece. **Mode** | As a cropping map is grayscale, the length is determined based on the level of darkness (RGB) or the transparency (Alpha). Transparent and black areas have the lowest Length, while opaque and white areas have the highest Length. **Level** | Adjust intensity of gray tones. Increasing the value makes the cropping effect more obvious. **Low/High Length** | Adjust the shortest or longest fur length. ** Trimming ** ** ** | **Intensity** | Trim the length from the edge to the center of the fur cluster. Higher intensity increases the difference in fur length from the edge to the center to create a sharper fur. #### ![Fur Cluster_4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192161561) **Random** | Higher randomization makes the clumps irregular, while lower randomization makes the clumps consistent. ![Fur Cluster_5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192161817) ** Bend Direction ** **** | ** Cluster ** | **Intensity** | Adjusts the intensity of the fur bending in each direction. Higher intensity makes the fur clump more pronounced and dimensional. ![Fur Cluster_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192162713) **Pores Density** | Adjust the pores density of the fur cluster. Higher density makes the clumps smaller and tighter, while lower density makes the clumps larger and more spread out. ![Fur Cluster_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211399065) **Direction/****Intensity Random** | Adjust whether the bend direction is consistent or irregular. ** Detail Cluster ** | The clumping of smaller sub-units within the cluster can be adjusted in the same way as the cluster. **Relax** | Adjust the intensity of clumping in detail clusters while keeping each direction intact. Higher relaxation makes the clumps loosen smoothly, as if gently combed out. ![Fur Cluster_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206211400473) #### #### **Fur Gravity** **Option** | ** Description ** ** ** ---|--- ** Force ** | Apply gravitational force. ** Vector ** | Manually apply a gravitational value to each axis. #### #### **Fur Curl** ** Option ** ** ** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Radius** | Configure the size of the curls. A higher value corresponds to larger curl and vice versa. Example (with Number 5.00): Radius = **5.00 vs. 1.00** ![Untitled_8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192165529) ![Untitled_9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192166041) **Number** | Configure the amount of curls. A higher value corresponds to more curls and vice versa. Example (with Radius 5.00): Number = **5.00 vs. 0.00** ![Untitled_8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192165529) ![Untitled_9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44206192166041) #### #### **Fur Variance** ** Option ** ** ** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Length** | Express uniform or irregular fur length. A higher value corresponds to more irregular fur length; lower value results in more uniform length variety. **Thickness** | Express uniform or irregular fur thickness. A higher value corresponds to more irregular fur thickness is; lower value results in more uniform thickness. **Direction** | Express uniform or irregular fur bending direction. A higher value corresponds to more irregular direction; lower value results in more uniform direction. **Gravity** | Express a uniform or irregular gravitational effect. A higher value causes a more irregular effect; lower value results in a more uniform effect. _A value can only be applied here if the Bending value is not 0._ #### #### **Fur Randomization** 1. Set the randomization properties. ** Option ** ** ** | ** Description ** ---|--- **Seed** | Obtain slightly different results with the same fur parameters. #### #### **Fur Export (USD)** 1. Access Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ **USD** 2. Select **Include Fur Strand Data. ****→** Export strand data with the USD file.
content_description: Discover the powerful new Fur Strand features in CLO 2025.0, enabling you to create and visualize realistic fur strands in various shapes and colors within the 3D window, while ensuring compatibility across different platforms.

title: glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) File
content: **List of Contents** Import Export Extensions **** Import or export glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) files.![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947024654617) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/NHUPJ8ceaqs) **** #### **Import** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Open Type** | Open or add new files. **Object Type** | **Load as Avatar / Trim** | Load a GLTF/GLB file as an avatar / trim. **Arrangement Points** **Auto Generate** | It automatically creates a Bounding Volume/Arrangement Points suitable for GLTF/GLB. **Scale** | Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. * Commonly used default unit for GLTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **** #### **Export** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ **glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired saving path and click **Save**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Object** | **Select All Avatars/ Patterns/ Graphics/ Trims** | Select or deselect objects to be exported. **Single/ Multiple Objects** | Export the object as a single or multiple objects. **Unweld/Weld** | Choose to export vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects or a single point. **Thick/Thin** | Choose to export the object with the thickness or not. **Combined UV Coordinates** | A combined UV coordinates are also exported. **Option** | **Light** **(Except for Render Lights)** | Export along with lights **Garment Animation** | Export garment's animation. **Avatar Animation** | ## ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947024656537) Export Joint or Cached avatar animation. **Scale** | Select the unit or the size of the object. * Commonly used default unit for GLTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **File** | **Save Colorway** | Choose whether you export colorway or not. Combine to One File/Multiple Files | Choose whether you combine all colorways into one file or create separate files for each colorway. **Save with glTF-Embedded (GLTF Only)** | Save textures as the glTF-Embedded format which includes texture files. **Save with Zip Files (ZIP)** **** | **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture** | When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting. **📝Note:** Since the color is diffused to the UV map when the Combined UV Coordinates is selected, the menu is hidden. **Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo)** | Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting.. **📝Note:** Since ambient maps and color are automatically excluded, the menu is hidden. **Save with MetaData (XML)** | Save garments' patterns (mesh), physical properties, and sewing information as MetaData (XML). **** #### **Extensions** **Property** | **Description** | **Required** ---|---|--- **Reflection Factor** | Reflection intensity of PBR material. In CLO, it has defaulted 15(0.15). Other engines and SW is defaulted 100(1.0) like the real world. | No, Default: 1.0
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing and exporting glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) files, including step-by-step instructions and configuration options.

title: Project File (ZPRJ) Open/Add/Save
content: #### **List of Contents** **Open or Add** **Save** #### All information, including garments, avatars, 3D environments(background, lighting, wind, camera and simulation), animations, and so on, can be saved and loaded as one project file(ZPRJ). #### #### **Open or Add** 1. Click Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open/Add ▶ **Project.** _* Open the file directly by dragging it from the OS Explorer to the 3D window or by right-clicking the file in CLO Library and clicking**Add to Workspace**. _ __ 2. Navigate and select the Project file to be added and click **Open**. 3. Apply any detailed settings, then click on the **OK** button. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Load Type** | Open a new project file or add the file additionally. If you add additional files, you can set the position of the object in the X, Y, and Z axis. **Object** | Select the contents to load within the project file. (Items that are not included will be disabled.) [**Colorway**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/32783140814105-Colorway) | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48730788207001) Choose specific colorways you want to open or add by clicking the ![Select Colorway.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48732648870041) **Select Colorway.**[**![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/50834108001689)**](https://youtu.be/BxfRrxCtaXc?si=6Rb38Qvse-yv7d86)![Thumbnail=On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48732696469017) _* The thumbnail for each colorway shows the fabric that is most extensively used in that garment. However, the files created in 2025.1 or eariler will show only colorway names, without thumnails._ **📝Note:** When adding colorways, if you add more colorways than currently exist, the current colorway will be automatically duplicated to fill the gap. The items added this way (fabrics, graphics, trims, etc.) will be linked, so you can choose to unlink either only the materials or all properties. **Display Settings** | Select **Display Settings** to open the project file with the saved [3D and 2D display settings](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29838353719321-Display-Setting-ver-2024-0). **📝 Note:** * If Display Settings is not selected, the display settings are reset to default. * When loading a previous file ver 2024.2 or before, Display Settings is deactivated. Please resave it in the new version for activating Display Settings. #### #### **Save** 1. Click Main Menu ▶ Save/Save As ▶**Project / Project (with Other Files)** 2. Set the location and name to save and click the **Save** button. 3. When saving as a project & other files, select the files ([Texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002686508-3D-Garment-Surface-Textures-Save), [DXF](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000493067-2D-Pattern-DXF-Import-Export), [PDF](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004273427-2D-Pattern-AI-PDF-Import-Export)) to be saved together and click the**OK** button.
